question.worked_solution:
We must factor the quadratic expression

$$
10{m}^{2}+13m+4.
$$

First, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant ($10\times 4=40$), and

- add to the linear coefficient ($13$).

Since all coefficients are positive, we only need to consider the positive factor pairs of $40.$

The positive factor pairs of $40$ are

$$
(1,40),\,(2,20),\,(4,10),\,(5,8).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(5,8)$ add to $13:$ 

$$
5+8=13\,✓
$$

Then, we write the linear term as $5m+8m,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}10{m}^{2}+13m+4 & = \\ 10{m}^{2}+5m+8m+4 & = \\ (10{m}^{2}+5m)+(8m+4) & = \\ 5m(2m+1)+4(2m+1) & = \\ (5m+4)(2m+1)\end{aligned}
$$
